data.title: The tumor suppressor CYLD acts as a deubiquitinase for mTOR to constrain its activity
data.authors: Fernandes SA; Pan J; Terziyska DS; Koyuncu S; Ding X; Németh IB; Wilhelm S; Nüchel J; Al-Gburi S; Gonidas C; Pasparakis M; Mosialos G; Széll M; Teleman AA; Eming SA; Vilchez D; Demetriades C

evidence.label: Preprint, not peer-reviewed
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Human cell lines (RNAi screen, CYLD loss of function); C. elegans cyld-1 knockdown in low-TORC1 lifespan mutants; skin biopsies from CYLD cutaneous syndrome patients
data.finding: An RNAi screen identified the tumor suppressor CYLD as a deubiquitinase that binds mTOR and removes non-degradative K63-linked ubiquitin chains from several of its residues, restraining both mTORC1 and mTORC2. Cells lacking CYLD show hyperactive mTORC1/2, higher protein synthesis, larger cell size and resistance to serum-starvation-induced cell death. In C. elegans, knocking down cyld-1 fully abolishes the extended lifespan of low-TORC1-activity mutants, and skin biopsies from CYLD cutaneous syndrome patients show mTORC1 hyperactivation. Preprint, not peer-reviewed.
data.abstract_excerpt: Proper control of mTOR (mechanistic/mammalian target of rapamycin) signaling is relevant for health, disease and ageing. Information from intra- and extra-cellular signaling cues is transmitted to mTOR through an intricate signaling network that impinges on the Rag and Rheb GTPases to regulate its localization and activity. Interestingly, although mTOR is a heavily ubiquitinated protein, the role of this post-translational modification (PTM) in regulating its activation status remains poorly understood.

extracted_findings.intervention: CYLD knockdown/loss of function; cyld-1 RNAi in C. elegans
